claim_1.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood samples from the first cohort of volunteers (n = 6 subjects/group) at days 0, 1, 3, 7, 10, 14, 21, and 28 after vaccination (day 0) showed that substantial changes in blood transcript abundance were detected after influenza vaccination compared to prevaccination levels.

sources.quote: This reveals, for instance, that most of the genes shown at day 7 and all of the genes at day 10 are induced by pneumococcal vaccination. It also shows both influenza and pneumococcal vaccines induce robust responses at day 1 postvaccination. This initial analysis indicates substantial changes in blood transcript abundance can be detected in response to these two non-live vaccines.

Figure 1. Blood Transcriptional Profiles of Vaccinated Subjects (A) Patterns of changes in transcript abundance are shown on a heatmap for a robust set of 239 transcripts using an FDR of 0.10 and fold change >2). For each subject, data are normalized to the average of the two baseline time points. Red represents relative increase in abundance, blue represents relative decrease, and yellow represents no change. (B) Lists of genes differentially expressed in response to each treatment for all time points or at each time point for all treatments are represented as segments on a circle.

claim_4.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood samples from the first cohort of volunteers (n = 6 subjects/group) at days 0, 1, 3, 7, 10, 14, 21, and 28 after vaccination (day 0) showed that transcript abundance changes were greatest at days 1 and 7 compared to the other sampled postvaccination time points.

sources.quote: Among the different time points, the majority of the changes were seen at days 1 and 7.

claim_5.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood from the influenza vaccine group at days 0, 1, 3, 7, 10, 14, 21, and 28 after vaccination (day 0), using modular repertoire analysis, showed responsive modules at day 1 compared to prevaccination levels.

sources.quote: Out of 62 modules, 17 and 14 passed this threshold at day 1 in the influenza vaccine and pneumococcal vaccine groups, respectively (Figure 2A).

Figure 2. Modular Mapping of the Global Changes in Blood Transcript Abundance Elicited by Vaccination Changes in transcript abundance measured in blood by using whole-genome arrays were mapped against a preconstructed modular analysis framework. The proportion of transcripts for which abundance was significantly changed in comparison to prevaccination levels was determined for each module. When this proportion exceeded the false discovery rate (set at 10%), the module was considered to be responsive to treatment. (A) The number of responsive modules is plotted on a graph at each time point for all three of the treatment groups.

claim_9.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood from the influenza vaccine and pneumococcal vaccine groups at days 0, 1, 3, 7, 10, 14, 21, and 28 after vaccination (day 0), using modular repertoire analysis, showed that these vaccines had different magnitudes of transcriptional responses at different time points compared to each other.

sources.quote: Thus, these two vaccines show different magnitudes of transcriptional responses at different time points after vaccination.

claim_10.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood from the influenza vaccine and pneumococcal vaccine groups at day 1 after vaccination (day 1), using modular repertoire analysis, showed increased modules M4.6, M6.6, and M6.13 and decreased modules M4.1, M4.15, M4.3, M5.11, and M6.9 compared to prevaccination levels in both vaccine groups.

sources.quote: Changes in eight modules were common to both vaccines, including increased modules M4.6 (functionally associated with inflammation), M6.6 and M6.13 (apoptosis/cell death) and decreased modules M4.1 and M4.15 (T cells), M4.3 (protein synthesis), M5.11, and M6.9 (no functional annotation).

claim_11.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood from the influenza vaccine group at day 1 after vaccination (day 1), using modular repertoire analysis, showed increased antiviral-response modules M1.2, M3.4, and M5.12 and the myeloid lineage and monocyte-associated module M4.14 compared to prevaccination levels.

sources.quote: Nine modules were uniquely responsive to the influenza vaccine. Of those, four were significantly increased and five were significantly decreased (Figure 3A; http://www.interactivefigures.com/dm3/vaccine-paper/figure-3.gsp). Three of the four increased modules were associated with antiviral responses (M1.2, M3.4, M5.12, Ingenuity Pathway Analysis enrichment p values)and included many genes coding for prototypical interferon (IFN)-inducible antiviral molecules such as OAS1, OAS2, OASL (M1.2); Guanylate Binding Proteins GBP1, GBP2, GBP4, GBP6 (M3.4); and TRIM family members such as TRIM5, TRIM21, TRIM25, TRIM38, TRIM56 (M5.12). The fourth increased module, M4.14, was associated with myeloid lineage and monocytes and includes, among others, genes coding for CD97, CD1D, interleukin-6 (IL-6), LY86, and CSF1R.

Figure 3. Functional Interpretation of Influenza and Pneumococcal Vaccine Day 1 Sig-natures Modules specifically responsive to the influenza (A) or pneumococcal (B) vaccines were subjected to pathway analysis. Only the genes within each module for which transcript abundance was significantly changed following vaccination were included in this analysis.

claim_12.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood from the influenza vaccine group at day 1 after vaccination (day 1), using modular repertoire analysis, showed decreased modules M3.6, M4.7, M4.8, M5.8, and M6.15 compared to prevaccination levels.

sources.quote: Modules that were decreased include M3.6 (natural killer cells and cytotoxicity), M4.7 (cell cycle), and three modules without definitive functional annotation (M4.8, M5.8, and M6.15).

claim_13.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood from the pneumococcal vaccine group at day 1 after vaccination (day 1), using modular repertoire analysis, showed increased inflammation-associated modules M3.2, M4.2, M4.13, M5.1, and M5.7 compared to prevaccination levels.

sources.quote: Six modules were uniquely responsive to the pneumococcal vaccine. Of these, five were modules including genes associated with inflammation (Figure 3B): M3.2 (e.g., CD63, IL-1RN, HMGB2, TLR4, TLR6, TLR8, as well as bcl-6), M4.2 (e.g., CR1, MMP9, TLR5), M4.13 (e.g., CD58, IL-8RA, CXCL1, and IL-1β), and M5.1 (e.g., CCR1, SERPINB8, MAPK1) and M5.7.

Figure 3. Functional Interpretation of Influenza and Pneumococcal Vaccine Day 1 Sig-natures Modules specifically responsive to the influenza (A) or pneumococcal (B) vaccines were subjected to pathway analysis. Only the genes within each module for which transcript abundance was significantly changed following vaccination were included in this analysis.

claim_14.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood from the pneumococcal vaccine group at day 1 after vaccination (day 1), using modular repertoire analysis, showed decreased module M4.12 compared to prevaccination levels.

sources.quote: Only one module, M4.12 (not annotated), was decreased.

claim_16.claim: Microarray analysis of capillary whole blood from an independent cohort (n = 6 subjects per group) at hours 0, 1.5, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 24, 36, and 48 after vaccination (day 0) showed that the influenza vaccine signature overlapped with transcripts induced by heat-inactivated gram-negative bacteria, heat-inactivated viruses (RSV, influenza), and IFN-γ compared to the saline control group.

sources.quote: The signature elicited within hours following immunization with seasonal influenza vaccine overlapped with transcripts induced by a small set of innate immune stimuli including heat-inactivated gram-negative bacteria, heat-inactivated viruses (RSV, influenza), and IFN-γ.

Figure 4. Mapping of the Response to Vaccines In Vivo and the Response to Innate Immune Ligands In Vitro Lists of genes differentially expressed at nine consecutive time points post vaccine administration or following in vitro treatment of blood for 6 hr with a wide range of innate stimuli are represented as segments of a circle. The degree of connectivity between the various segments on this plot indicates the degree of overlap between in vivo- and in vitro-derived gene lists.

claim_17.claim: Microarray analysis of capillary whole blood from an independent cohort (n = 6 subjects per group) at hours 0, 1.5, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 24, 36, and 48 after vaccination (day 0) showed that the influenza vaccine overlapping transcript set was dominated by interferon-inducible genes including EGR1, ADAR, Fcγ receptors, GBP1, GBP2, IFI16, HLX, IRF1, IRF9, STAT1, TAP1, TLR7, and TRAIL compared to the saline control group.

sources.quote: The overlapping gene transcript set was dominated by interferon-inducible genes, including the transcription factor EGR1, ADAR (RNA-editing enzyme that deaminates adenosines and modifies viral genomes), Fcγ receptors, GBP1 and GBP2 (IFN-inducible, specifically bind guanine nucleotides), IFI16 (amplifier in intracellular DNA recognition response), HLX (transcription factor involved in T helper 1 cell (Th1)-type response polarization), IRF1 and IRF9 (transcription factors involved in type I IFN production and IFN signaling), STAT1 (transcription factor that mediates the IFN response), TAP1 (involved in antigen presentation via MHCI), TLR7(receptor for single stranded RNA) and TRAIL (TNFSF10, involved in induction of apoptosis).

claim_18.claim: Microarray analysis of capillary whole blood from an independent cohort (n = 6 subjects per group) at hours 0, 1.5, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 24, 36, and 48 after vaccination (day 0) showed that the pneumococcal vaccine signature overlapped with in vitro signatures induced by heat-inactivated bacteria, LPS, flagellin, PAM3, R837, zymosan, CpG, IFN-γ, and IL-18 compared to the saline control group.

sources.quote: The pneumococcal vaccine signature overlapped with in vitro signature induced by heat-inactivated bacteria, LPS, flagellin, PAM3, R837, zymosan, CpG, IFN-γ, IL-18.

Figure 4. Mapping of the Response to Vaccines In Vivo and the Response to Innate Immune Ligands In Vitro Lists of genes differentially expressed at nine consecutive time points post vaccine administration or following in vitro treatment of blood for 6 hr with a wide range of innate stimuli are represented as segments of a circle. The degree of connectivity between the various segments on this plot indicates the degree of overlap between in vivo- and in vitro-derived gene lists.

claim_19.claim: Microarray analysis of capillary whole blood from an independent cohort (n = 6 subjects per group) at hours 0, 1.5, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 24, 36, and 48 after vaccination (day 0) showed that the pneumococcal vaccine overlapping transcript set included IL-1B, IL-1RN, IL-6R, ADM, FCGR2A, TRAIL, CASP4, IRF2, BCL3, VAV1, BCL6, and ETS2 compared to the saline control group.

sources.quote: The overlapping gene transcript set included IL-1B, IL-1RN, IL-6R, ADM (a vasodilatator), FCGR2A, TRAIL and CASP4 (apoptosis inducers), IRF2 (inhibits IRF1-mediated IFN induction and binds to the IL7 promoter), and transcription factors BCL3 (NF-κB signaling), VAV1 (Rho signaling), BCL6, and ETS2 (leukocyte differentiation and/or proliferation).

claim_20.claim: Microarray analysis of capillary whole blood from an independent cohort (n = 6 subjects per group) at hours 0, 1.5, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 24, 36, and 48 after vaccination (day 0) showed that vaccine responses were detectable in blood within hours after administration compared to baseline (hour 0).

sources.quote: This analysis demonstrates that vaccines act as potent activators of the innate immune system and that responses can be detected in the blood in vivo within hours following administration.

claim_21.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood from influenza vaccine recipients at hours 0, 1.5, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 24, 36, and 48 after vaccination (day 0), using modular analysis, showed that the IFN response module M1.2 changed significantly as early as 15 hr after vaccination compared to baseline (hour 0).

sources.quote: Significant changes in the transcription of genes forming IFN response module were observed as early as 15 hr following administration of the vaccine and persisted to 48 hr postvaccination.

Figure 5. Profiling the Interferon Response within the First 48 hr following Vaccination (A) Baseline-normalized whole-blood expression levels of genes forming module M1.2 (IFN-inducible gene module) were averaged and plottedonagraph. Values are shown at multiple consecutive time points for the influenza vaccine and saline control groups.

claim_23.claim: Microarray analysis of neutrophils and monocytes isolated from the blood of influenza vaccine recipients (n = 6) at 24 hr after vaccination (day 1) showed differences in expression of IFN-inducible transcripts compared to prevaccination levels.

sources.quote: The analysis revealed differences in the levels of expression for IFN-inducible transcripts in neutrophils and in monocytes following influenza vaccination (module-level data shown in Figure 5B; http://www.interactivefigures.com/dm3/vaccine-paper/figure-5.gsp).

Figure 5. Profiling the Interferon Response within the First 48 hr following Vaccination (B) Baseline-normalized expression levels of genes forming module M1.2 were averaged and plotted on a graph. Values are shown for different cell populations isolated from the blood of subjects24 hr postvaccination.

claim_24.claim: Luminex analysis of sera from influenza vaccine recipients at day 1 after vaccination (day 1) showed that CXCL10 (IP-10) levels increased compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: Furthermore, serum levels of the IFN-inducible chemokine CXCL10 (IP-10) were also found to increase significantly on day 1 after influenza vaccination (p < 0.01; Figure S4).

claim_25.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood and isolated leukocyte populations from influenza vaccine recipients showed that influenza vaccination induced an early type I interferon signature in blood carried by neutrophils and monocytes compared to prevaccination levels.

sources.quote: Thus, administration of the influenza vaccine leads to early type I interferon signature in the blood carried by neutrophils and monocytes.

claim_26.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood from the influenza vaccine group at day 7 after vaccination (day 7), using modular analysis, showed increased abundance of transcripts in plasma cell precursor module M4.11 compared to prevaccination levels.

sources.quote: At day 7, the abundance of 35% of the transcripts forming module M4.11 increased significantly in comparison to prevaccination levels in the influenza vaccine group.

Plasma Cell Precursor Immune Signature (A) Baseline-normalized whole blood expression levels of genes forming module M4.11 (plasma cell precursors module) were averaged and plotted on a graph. Values are shown at multiple consecutive time points for the influenza vaccine, pneumococcal vaccine and saline control groups.

claim_27.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood from the pneumococcal vaccine group at day 7 after vaccination (day 7), using modular analysis, showed increased abundance of transcripts in plasma cell precursor module M4.11 compared to prevaccination levels.

sources.quote: In the pneumococcal vaccine group, 70% of the M4.11 transcripts were significantly increased.

Figure 6. claim_29.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood from the pneumococcal vaccine group at day 7 after vaccination (day 7), using modular analysis, showed that modules M3.3 and M4.9 were responsive only after pneumococcal vaccination compared to prevaccination levels.

sources.quote: Two other modules, M3.3 and M4.9, were responsive to pneumococcal vaccination only at day 7 (data not shown).

claim_30.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of whole blood samples from influenza vaccine recipients at days 0, 1, 3, 7, 10, 14, 21, and 28 after vaccination (day 0) showed that plasmablast absolute numbers increased at day 7 compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: This increase was significant at day 7 following administration of the influenza vaccine and on days 7 and 10 following administration of the pneumococcal vaccine.

Figure 6. Plasma Cell Precursor Immune Signature (B) Abundance of plasmablasts measured by multi-parameter flow cytometry is plotted on a graph. Values are shown at multiple consecutive time points for the influenza vaccine, pneumococcal vaccine and saline control groups.
